assumptions_challenged: Rodent intranasal biodistribution reliably predicts intact‑EV CNS exposure in larger species
Existing program analytics are sufficient to distinguish intact EV from non‑vesicular signal in handling, device delivery, and in vivo matrices
Current small‑scale materials and procedures are adequate to support formulation advancement without an MCB/WCB and multiple scaled GMP‑like batches
Formulation/excipient/device choices will not disrupt EV identity during handling and nasal administration
Program preference for a single bridging large species (e.g., NHP) is required rather than a data‑driven species selection
falsification_conditions: Establish a characterized source cell with MCB/WCB and documentary process controls for production

Develop orthogonal QC panel (particles, protein, lipid markers per MISEV) and demonstrate analytical validation at least fit‑for‑purpose including LLOQs, specificity, and precision for intact‑EV assays
Demonstrate mechanism‑linked potency assay(s) that are stability‑indicating and show correlation with relevant in vivo PD endpoints
Produce ≥3 representative GMP‑like scale‑up batches showing reproducible release assay results, potency, and stability in accelerated and real‑time studies (predefined acceptance criteria met)

Show formulation/device compatibility with quantitative intact‑EV recovery and identity preservation after handling and simulated/real device administration (ex vivo nasal model and in vivo), using disrupted‑EV and free‑label controls to exclude artefactual signal

Obtain bridging in vivo PK/biodistribution in rodent and a prespecified large species showing reproducible intact‑EV CNS exposure vs controls within predefined PK variability and exposure acceptance limits
strongest_objection: Do not advance a specific intranasal formulation into higher‑confidence delivery testing yet because the program lacks validated, orthogonal analytics, MCB/WCB and demonstrated process reproducibility/stability, and any intact‑EV CNS exposure across species — without those CMC and assay de‑risks, formulation compatibility and in vivo bridging studies cannot reliably assess intact‑EV delivery or mechanism.
